Things to Know: Prior to Travel Request

From the ORA eTraining module "Travel on Sponsored Projects: From Approval to Reimbursement" (lesson 1 of 8).
Greetings MSU Faculty and Staff!
Traveling on grant funding is a valuable opportunity to expand your research network, collaborate with leading experts, and gain exposure to cutting-edge practices in your field. Before we jump into travel procedures for MSU-organized travel please review the important information below.
Complete the content above before moving on.
Things to Know: Prior to Travel Form Submission
Destination details & allocability
Where are you going on the trip? How long will you be there? Why are you going there? Is this travel related to your project's scope of work?
Estimated Expenses
Think about what costs you will incur over the course of this trip: Conference registration fees Hotel/Lodging Flight or Train ticket Meal costs per diem Please Note: You cannot claim per diem for meals offered by a conference while on University travel. When submitting reimbursement, MSU's travel office will compare requested per diem reimbursements with conference itineraries to determine allowability. Ground Transportation (personal vehicle mileage, taxi/uber, tolls, hotel/airport parking, etc)
Index & Budget
Be sure to use the correct Banner index on travel forms, as provided by the RFA team at project setup. Also, check your budget to ensure you have enough funds in the 04: Travel pool.
p-card Purchases
Many travel expenses may be charged to your University Purchasing Card, helping to minimize the need for out-of-pocket payments and reduce reliance on travel reimbursements. Such expenses may include: Conference Registration Fees Hotel/Lodging Uber/Taxi Parking
